transcript.statement: Sustainability is crucial for modern software systems. My requirements (GRN-01 to GRN-07) ensure that the RollCall system minimizes energy consumption, utilizes efficient storage, and promotes low-power operations, which can significantly reduce its carbon footprint. GRN-01 encourages energy-efficient algorithms, while GRN-02 focuses on sustainable cloud solutions. GRN-03 ensures real-time updates with low-energy protocols, and GRN-04 aims to minimize digital resource usage. These measures align with growing environmental concerns. Furthermore, GRN-05 raises awareness of carbon footprints, and GRN-06 ensures responsible data retention. GRN-07 optimizes the user experience on low-power devices, making the system more accessible and sustainable.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is vital for the RollCall system, ensuring that attendance data is processed quickly and accurately. My requirements (EFF-01 to EFF-07) prioritize real-time processing, responsiveness, and the ability to handle multiple users without degradation. For instance, EFF-01 guarantees updates within 2 seconds, while EFF-03 ensures reports are generated swiftly, making the system effective for both teachers and students. However, I recognize potential conflicts with GRN-01 and GRN-02, as real-time processing may lead to higher energy consumption, contradicting sustainability goals. I also see a conflict with SAF-04 and RES-07 regarding the historical data storage that could strain resources.

transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is paramount for the RollCall system, as it deals with sensitive student attendance data. My requirements (TRU-01 to TRU-07) ensure robust security measures are in place. TRU-01 mandates encryption of data to protect it both at rest and in transit, while TRU-02 establishes role-based access control to prevent unauthorized access. TRU-03 ensures that all modifications are logged for accountability, and TRU-04 restricts student access to their records only after authentication. TRU-05 implements integrity checks to safeguard data accuracy, and TRU-06 provides mechanisms for reporting breaches. Finally, TRU-07 enforces session timeouts to enhance security. However, I recognize potential conflicts with efficiency and sustainability, particularly in requirements related to data access and processing speed.

transcript.statement: Safety and reliability are critical for the RollCall system to protect sensitive attendance data from unauthorized access and ensure data accuracy. My requirements (SAF-01 to SAF-07) establish secure authentication (SAF-01), real-time data synchronization (SAF-02), and automated alerts for discrepancies (SAF-03) to enhance reliability. Storing historical data for five years (SAF-04) supports long-term analysis, while logging modifications (SAF-05) ensures accountability. Manual overrides (SAF-06) maintain system reliability during failures, and regular security audits (SAF-07) identify vulnerabilities. However, I see conflicts with efficiency (EFF-01, EFF-03), as real-time processing may compromise safety if not managed carefully, and historical data storage (SAF-04) could strain resources, impacting performance.

transcript.statement: Ethical and compliance considerations are essential for the RollCall system. However, I acknowledge potential conflicts with efficiency (EFF-01, EFF-03) due to the need for quick processing, which might compromise compliance and transparency. requirements.text: The system shall ensure secure authentication of users to prevent unauthorized access to attendance data.
The system shall provide real-time data synchronization with a maximum processing time of 2.5 seconds during peak loads.
The system shall implement automated alerts for discrepancies in attendance reporting to ensure data accuracy.
The system shall store historical attendance data for a minimum of 4 years while ensuring compliance with GDPR.
The system shall provide a logging mechanism for all attendance modifications to support accountability and traceability.
The system shall prioritize security measures during peak loads to ensure encryption effectiveness and data integrity.
The system shall support cloud storage solutions that prioritize energy-efficient data centers.
The system shall allow students to view their attendance records with a response time of under 3 seconds.
The system shall implement optimized algorithms for real-time processing to minimize latency.
The system shall allow students to dispute attendance records through a formal process within 10 days of marking.
The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR when handling student attendance data.
The system shall provide transparency in attendance recording by logging all attendance changes with timestamps.
The system shall implement role-based access control to restrict data access based on user roles.
